decisions.decision: Use a three-column editorial video grid on desktop and a horizontal scroll-snap rail on phones and tablets; tapping a project opens a full video-and-details dialog.
decisions.reason: Most visitors arrive from Instagram on touch devices, so the interaction must be obvious, swipeable and comfortable at phone and tablet sizes while preserving the site's monochrome editorial language.

decisions.decision: On iPhone, make the entire video-detail backdrop the scroll container and provide large explicit mute and fullscreen controls below the player.
decisions.reason: Mobile Safari reserves continuous volume for device controls and its native fullscreen affordance is small, so the web UI should expose reliable mute and fullscreen actions without trapping the project text below the viewport.

decisions.decision: Animate the home hero heading with React Bits FoldText while preserving its existing black editorial typography, and reveal the supporting copy with a separate left-to-right entrance.
decisions.reason: The title gains the requested paper-fold motion without changing the established layout, while the independently timed subtitle keeps the hierarchy clear and the two elements visually distinct.

decisions.decision: Reveal the portfolio heading and dark contact call-to-action with one-time, staggered horizontal entrances driven by IntersectionObserver and CSS transforms.
decisions.reason: The additional motion gives both editorial sections a clear entrance while remaining lightweight, compositor-friendly and respectful of reduced-motion preferences.
